cases.rationale: Regional beech forests may fit deciduous temperate forests, but soil and assemblage distinctions must remain.
cases.requiredEvidence: Canopy composition, seasonal climate, source diagnostic flora and extent.

cases.rationale: Raised and blanket bog morphology should not replace the broader functional bog description.
cases.requiredEvidence: Hydrological source, peat processes, climatic applicability and local interpretations.

cases.rationale: Fen groupings share mineral-water context but differ in chemistry, flora and geographical support.
cases.requiredEvidence: Water source, base status, carbonate chemistry, peat extent and diagnostic assemblages.

cases.rationale: A tall-helophyte bed is not automatically a permanently inundated functional marsh.
cases.requiredEvidence: Hydroperiod, productivity, substrate, geomorphic support and stand extent.

cases.rationale: Similar grass cover can retain different flora, substrate and management meanings.
cases.requiredEvidence: Climate, seasonal water balance, soils, management history and vegetation diagnostics.

cases.rationale: An intensive unmixed crop class might fit annual cropland when its crop cycle and management agree.
cases.requiredEvidence: Annual versus perennial cycle, crop identity, management intensity and land-use extent.

cases.rationale: Fast perennial water is not sufficient to infer upland stream context.
cases.requiredEvidence: Stream order, slope, flow variability, catchment support and watercourse boundaries.

cases.rationale: Seasonal variation can occur in perennial as well as temporary upland streams.
cases.requiredEvidence: Observed cycle, flow cessation, residual pools, seasonal amplitude and reference window.

cases.rationale: GET lake size/permanence and EUNIS trophic status partition different dimensions.
cases.requiredEvidence: Area, freshwater chemistry, permanence, trophic measurements and mixing regime.

cases.rationale: Saline, brackish and soda lake categories need different chemistry and connectivity tests.
cases.requiredEvidence: Salinity definition, ionic composition, alkalinity, ocean connection and water persistence.

cases.rationale: Regional littoral rock may refine a global rocky-shoreline context without changing the underlying function.
cases.requiredEvidence: Tidal limits, wave exposure, community evidence and source-region applicability.

cases.rationale: Regional seagrass community classes are candidates, not automatic synonyms for the global functional group.
cases.requiredEvidence: Species assemblage, meadow structure, substrate, tidal setting, light and spatial support.

cases.rationale: A rock class can contain kelp ecosystems but need not be a kelp forest.
cases.requiredEvidence: Canopy-forming kelps, functional community, temperature/light and spatial extent.

cases.rationale: The selected EUNIS example is littoral mud whereas GET M1.8 is subtidal; mud identity alone cannot establish equivalence.
cases.requiredEvidence: A compatible subtidal EUNIS target and explicit tidal/bathymetric support. No logical disjointness is asserted.

cases.rationale: Neuston is an air-sea-interface community, not the complete epipelagic water-column system.
cases.requiredEvidence: Part/whole or interface relationship, depth/light structure and co-occurrence rather than equivalence.

cases.rationale: Arctic sea-ice communities may be a regional instance of global sea-ice functioning.
cases.requiredEvidence: Sea-ice rather than terrestrial ice, sympagic biota, seasonality and regional applicability.
